entities.summary:
Elim mac Conrach was a High King of Ireland, according to medieval Irish legend and historical tradition, ruling over the kingdom of Dal Riata in the 4th century.

    He was the son of Conrai, a powerful king of Dal Riata, and is often mentioned alongside his father in the Ulster Cycle, a collection of Irish mythological tales.

    Elim's reign is believed to have been marked by conflict with neighboring kingdoms, including the kingdom of Ulster, which would later become a major power in Ireland.

    The legacy of Elim mac Conrach can be seen in the continued influence of the Ulster Cycle on Irish literature and culture, with his name remaining a prominent figure in Irish history and mythology.
